name: Esther Leon

positions.statement: On her campaign website, León says Portlanders are overtaxed and underdelivered.
On her campaign website's property tax reform section, León proposes a Land Value Tax that taxes only the value of the land.
positions.excerpt: Land Value Tax, in which only the value of the land is taxed, not the value of the property resting on the land.

positions.statement: On her campaign website, León says she would direct focus toward long-term housing stability for the highest-need houseless residents.
positions.excerpt: Directing focus toward long-term housing stability for our highest need houseless neighbors

positions.statement: On her campaign website, León lists redirecting efforts away from practices like city sweeps and hostile architecture.
positions.excerpt: Redirecting efforts away from practices like city sweeps and hostile architecture,

positions.statement: On her campaign website's health care section, León says health care is a human right.
On her campaign website, León supports a combination of housing and health and/or substance treatment for high-need houseless residents.
positions.excerpt: a combo of housing + health and/or substance treatment

positions.statement: On her campaign website, León proposes funding free Spanish, Vietnamese, Chinese and Russian language classes at Portland Community College.
positions.excerpt: Funding free Spanish, Vietnamese, Chinese, and Russian

positions.statement: On her campaign website, León proposes on-site child care for government employees to make it easier for parents to be public servants.
positions.excerpt: Offering on-site childcare for government employees to make it easier for parents to be public servants.

positions.statement: On her campaign website's environment section, León proposes a moratorium on AI data centers, citing the takeover of natural resources.
positions.excerpt: Implementing a moratorium on AI data centers to stop the takeover of natural resources.

positions.statement: On her campaign website's transportation section, León lists expanding bus and light rail hours to past bar closing time.
positions.excerpt: Expanding bus and light rail hours to past bar closing time

positions.statement: On her campaign website, León proposes paying city janitorial staff a living wage to keep park restrooms clean and open year-round.
positions.excerpt: Paying city janitorial staff a living wage to keep park restrooms clean and open 365 days a year.

positions.statement: On her campaign website's health care section, León says most small business owners cannot afford to provide their employees with benefits.
positions.excerpt: Most small business owners simply cannot afford to provide their employees with benefits.

positions.statement: On her campaign website, León proposes living wage paid work for houseless residents collecting trash in public spaces.
positions.excerpt: Offering our houseless neighbors the dignity of living wage paid work for collecting trash in public spaces.

positions.statement: On her campaign website's public safety section, León says Portland Police Bureau needs to acknowledge harmful practices used to target marginalized groups.
positions.excerpt: Portland Police Bureau needs to acknowledge the harmful practices it has utilized to target marginalized groups

positions.statement: On her campaign website, León pledges not to take contributions from police unions or associations.
positions.excerpt: I pledge not to take contributions from police unions or associations

collection_notes: All 15 items come from the campaign site estherforportland.com (T2), whose domain is confirmed via the county pamphlet statement. Two WebFetches of the same page (cached). Searches for the six remaining issues surfaced no page naming her on those topics. Identity: the site and the pamphlet filing both list the same candidate (physical therapist, Portland District 3).
